🇲🇽📚 <u>Strapped to a Chair: Nuevo León Schools Are Still Failing Autistic Kids</u>

Nuevo León's state human rights commission issued two recommendations over the treatment of six students with autism and other conditions. One was a 10-year-old whose teacher strapped him to his chair with a belt to keep him from standing up in class. Writing in Contralínea, Ana María Ibarra Olguín notes that Mexico already has inclusive-education guidelines and guides for neurodivergent students. Making them work takes institutional effort, she writes, "from teacher training to the (un)availability of resources in schools." UNESCO has found that well-planned inclusion helps prevent stereotyping and stigma for every child in the room.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>As Oil Eases, Hacienda Trims the Diesel Subsidy by 38.84%</u>

With crude prices falling, Mexico's Finance Ministry cut the special diesel subsidy for November 7-13 from 2.60 to 1.59 pesos per liter, a drop of 38.84%. The tax break itself stays whole: the federal government still absorbs 100% of the IEPS fuel tax on diesel, so drivers pay zero pesos of it per liter. Under the voluntary agreement with fuel retailers, diesel stays capped at 27 pesos a liter. Magna gasoline gets a 26.01% IEPS stimulus, and Premium gets 24.51%.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico Wishes Paraguay's New President Success After Peña's Fall</u>

Mexico's Foreign Ministry greeted Pedro Alliana on Saturday as Paraguay's new president. Paraguay's Senate had removed Santiago Peña in a fast-track impeachment over the collapse of Ueno Bank, and Peña is now under investigation for influence peddling and breach of trust. The SRE wished Alliana success for the good of the Paraguayan people and said Mexico "maintains its willingness to continue strengthening relations of friendship and cooperation with Paraguay and the governments of Latin America and the Caribbean." A day earlier, Sheinbaum had drawn the lesson from the scandal: economic power and political power have to be kept apart.

🇲🇽🎨 "I have always thought, since I studied physics and then engineering, that engineering is for transforming the world, the same as politics. Good politics is the one we do to transform people's lives, to generate well-being, to generate justice." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Suchiapa, Chiapas She told engineering students that President Lázaro Cárdenas founded the Instituto Politécnico Nacional with the motto "technology in the service of the homeland." Showing a picture of the Rizo de Oro bridge she had opened that morning, designed and built by Mexican engineers, she said it is "not only a marvelous technical advance, it is not only very beautiful, it is also social justice," because people who crossed by raft in one or two hours will now cross in five minutes. "That is Mexican engineering. That is you." The Universidad Politécnica de Chiapas has 3,234 students in 10 engineering programs.
banner: "TECHNOLOGY IN THE SERVICE OF THE HOMELAND"

text: 🇲🇽🎨 "In the 60s they called young people troublemakers. Then in the 90s, during the neoliberal period, they called them ninis. From 2006 to 2018 they called them sicarios. Today all the young people of the country are becarios, because that is where they should be, in the schools." — Mario Delgado, Secretary of Public Education, Suchiapa, Chiapas "Ninis": neither studying nor working. "Sicarios": hitmen. "Becarios": scholarship holders. Delgado said governments stopped building high schools and universities even as Mexico was about to have the most young people in its history. In the last 30 years, 20 technological high schools were built; in just 2 years, Sheinbaum is building more than double that. The Tlalpan mansion of former police chief Arturo "El Negro" Durazo, with a heliport and a greyhound track, "a monument to corruption," will become a Rosario Castellanos national university campus.

🇲🇽✊ "Where does that money come from? How is it that the government can now support people and before it couldn't? Because now taxes are collected from those who must pay them, and now there is no robbing." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, La Concordia, Chiapas "Before, there were no scholarships for girls, boys, young people. At most a few for a select few. The vote was requested in exchange for support. Not now. Now it is universal." In Chiapas every public school student, from primary through university, now has a scholarship. The universal pension for older adults, begun in 2019, and the pension for people with disabilities are constitutional rights, and the pension must rise above inflation every year. More than 400,000 farmers receive Sembrando Vida. "That is the Fourth Transformation of public life."

🇲🇽✊ "Abroad they boasted that the only opportunity Mexico had was to offer cheap labor. Not how good Mexican workers were, not the culture of Mexicans. To foreign investment, they offered cheap labor." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, La Concordia, Chiapas At the Rizo de Oro bridge on November 7, she said La Angostura dam was finished in 1976: "a hydroelectric plant was built for the well-being of Mexico, but the people were forgotten." She named the six presidents of the neoliberal period, 1982 to 2018: De la Madrid, Salinas, Zedillo, Fox, Calderón, Peña Nieto. "The minimum wage did not rise." Public companies were sold to a few at the top. From 1943 to 1982, about 27,000 IMSS hospital beds were built; in the following 36 years, only 4,000. "We must not forget it, because a people without memory has no compass."
banner: "A PEOPLE WITHOUT MEMORY HAS NO COMPASS"

text: 🇲🇽✊ "They could not travel by road because they were afraid of the people. They thought that reaching the presidency meant moving away from the people. And we think the opposite." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Suchiapa, Chiapas "The presidents of long ago did not do this. They stayed locked up in the president's house of the time, which was Los Pinos." When they went out, they were surrounded by the Estado Mayor Presidencial: "8,000 soldiers dedicated to guarding the president." Los Pinos became a museum open to the public when López Obrador took office. Sheinbaum tours the states every Friday to Sunday, sometimes from Thursday: "The job of a president is to listen, attend and resolve." This weekend: Chiapa de Corzo and Ocozocoautla on Friday, then on Saturday the Rizo de Oro bridge, three hours from Tuxtla, and the scholarship event in Suchiapa.

🇲🇽🎨 "In all of Latin America, those who led independence were criollo military men... But in Mexico, independence was commanded by a village priest, Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla, and his disciple José María Morelos y Pavón. They did not only fight for independence, they fought for social justice." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Suchiapa, Chiapas At the Universidad Politécnica de Chiapas on November 7, she told students that Morelos wrote a Constitution, Apatzingán's, that never took effect but is the basis of the 1917 Constitution. In it: "Education must be the same for the son of the hacendado as for the son of the peon." "We must moderate indigence and opulence." And the sovereignty of the homeland "did not lie in a few, but resided in the people of Mexico." "There is no country in the world like ours."

🇲🇽🚆 "They told him, 'Mr. President, from here we have to go on horseback, because there is no road.' And he said, 'How is it possible that the state of Chiapas is not connected?'" — Governor Eduardo Ramírez, La Concordia, Chiapas Opening the Rizo de Oro bridge, the governor recalled that in 1940 President Lázaro Cárdenas toured Oaxaca and then Chiapas, riding on horseback all the way to the Soconusco. Out of that trip came the Pan-American Highway through Chiapas to Central America. Then in the 1970s the La Angostura dam flooded the old town of La Concordia and split the families of the Sierra from those of the Frailesca. For decades they asked for bridges. "Many years had to pass for Chiapas to become the national priority." From Chicomuselo to Tuxtla, a trip of more than 5 hours will now take about 2.5.
